annotations.title: Dawn of the Space Age - NASA

content.text:
Assuming you mean **the first artificial satellite vs a modern “latest” satellite**:

| Feature | First satellite: **Sputnik 1** | Latest modern satellites, e.g. **Starlink / Amazon Leo / modern Earth-observation sats** |
|---|---|---|
| **Launch date** | **October 4, 1957** | Ongoing; satellites are launched almost every week. For example, SpaceX listed a Starlink mission for **June 8, 2026**, and Arianespace announced 36 Amazon Leo satellites planned for **June 17, 2026**. ([nasa.gov](https://www.nasa.gov/history/dawn-of-the-space-age/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Country / operator** | Soviet Union | Many: SpaceX, Amazon, NASA, ESA, China, India, private companies, militaries |
| **Size / mass** | 58 cm diameter; **83.6 kg** | Varies hugely: small CubeSats under 10 kg to large telecom satellites of several tons |
| **Main purpose** | Prove an artificial object could orbit Earth; transmitted simple radio “beeps” | Internet service, GPS/navigation, weather, military surveillance, climate monitoring, imaging, science, communications |
| **Technology** | Simple radio transmitter, batteries, antennas | Solar power, computers, AI/autonomy, electric propulsion, high-speed communications, cameras/radar, laser links |
| **Lifetime** | About 3 months before re-entry | Often 5–15+ years, depending on orbit and design |
| **Data capability** | Very basic radio signal | Gigabits of data, high-resolution images, global broadband, real-time Earth monitoring |
| **Impact** | Started the Space Age and helped trigger the Space Race | Satellites now support daily life: internet, phone networks, banking timing, maps, weather forecasts, disaster response |

**In simple terms:**  
**Sputnik 1 was like a tiny beeping metal ball proving spaceflight was possible.** Modern satellites are more like **orbiting computers, cameras, cell towers, and scientific labs** that provide internet, navigation, weather data, and Earth monitoring.
